details: Market expectations for a potential interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve in December are intensifying, fueled by higher-than-expected inflation data for October across the Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), and Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE). This hawkish outlook is pushing up the US dollar and making non-yielding assets like cryptocurrencies less attractive. Concurrently, US spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) have experienced significant outflows, with some reports indicating over $1.91 billion in net redemptions over seven consecutive trading days, further reducing liquidity and contributing to a broad cryptocurrency sell-off. Bitcoin has fallen to its lowest levels since August 2026, dropping below key psychological and technical support levels.
title: US Rate Hike Fears and Bitcoin ETF Outflows Drive Crypto Downturn

details: Federal Reserve officials are increasingly concerned that the booming Artificial Intelligence (AI) sector, particularly significant spending on AI infrastructure, is contributing to inflationary pressures. This new source of inflation could lead to the central bank maintaining higher interest rates for a more extended period than previously anticipated. Elevated interest rates tend to divert capital away from speculative assets such as cryptocurrencies, making traditional interest-bearing investments more appealing. The ongoing AI-driven demand for resources is transforming technology from a deflationary force into a key driver of inflation, posing a dilemma for policymakers aiming to control rising prices.
title: AI Boom's Inflationary Impact Could Keep Rates Higher for Longer
